clue.text: Fish out of water, without oxygen

indicators.note: without here means outside of, so the dry letters sit around the oxygen symbol

parts.note: something out of water is dry
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A fish flapping about out of water, starved of oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense 'outside', not 'lacking': DRY goes round O. The surface makes oxygen look like what the fish is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: The John Dory is an edible sea fish, usually just called a dory.

clue.text: Legal document by which one's recalled

definitions.text: Legal document by which one's recalled

parts.words: Legal document by which one's recalled
parts.note: recalled read as re-called: the paper by which a person formally takes a new name and is called something else from then on

explanation.surface: A legal paper that brings someone back, as if summoning a recalled official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' suggests remembering or being summoned back; read it as 're-called', called by a new name, which is what this deed achieves.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed poll is the British legal instrument used to change one's name officially.

clue.text: Daisy's family member, a kid Bruce abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned suggests behaving wildly without restraint, which signals the letters being thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A child left behind by a man called Bruce, set against a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' reads as deserted but is the anagram signal: A KID BRUCE rearranged gives the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudbeckias, the coneflowers or black-eyed Susans, belong to the aster family, Asteraceae, the daisy family.

clue.text: Staunch support

definitions.meaning: to staunch is to stop a flow, as of blood
a supporting stalk, as of a plant or wine glass

explanation.definitionFit: Stopping a flow of blood is stemming it, and a stalk holding up a flower or glass bowl is its stem.

clue.text: A dozen in a box, in most cases

definitions.text: A dozen in a box, in most cases

parts.words: A dozen in a box, in most cases
parts.note: a box of a dozen suggests eggs, but the box is a courtroom's jury box, where twelve citizens hear most trials

explanation.surface: A dozen items packed into a box, as with eggs, usually.
explanation.walkthrough: The box is the jury box and the cases are court cases; the answer is the traditional phrase for an English jury of twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the time-honoured description of a jury of twelve honest citizens.

clue.text: Note in outdated currency

definitions.meaning: to note something is to take notice of it, heed it
the German currency replaced by the euro in 2002

explanation.surface: A banknote in a currency no longer used.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed something is to mark it, and the Deutschmark was Germany's money before the euro.

clue.text: Person who's just come, say, to a part of Africa

indicators.note: say signals that the newcomer's word is spoken, and its sound is written another way

parts.note: a newbie is someone who has just arrived or started

explanation.surface: A newcomer heading for a region of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWBIE spoken sounds like NUBI, and A follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubia is the ancient region along the Nile in southern Egypt and northern Sudan.

clue.text: Emperor in line cut short in chaos following revolution

indicators.note: a revolution overturns things, so the pooled letters are thrown into a new order
the word line is cut down to its opening letter only

explanation.surface: An emperor next in line whose reign is cut short amid revolutionary chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' trims 'line' to its first letter, and 'following revolution' rearranges the pooled letters. Fittingly, Tsar Nicholas II fell in the Russian Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas II was the last Russian tsar, the emperor deposed in 1917.

clue.text: Aromatic plant is put in experimental place facing north

indicators.note: in a down clue, facing north means reading upwards, so the built word is turned backwards
put in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: a lab is a place where experiments are done

explanation.surface: A fragrant herb is planted in an experimental garden facing north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' makes LISAB; in a down clue 'facing north' means reading upwards, which turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a fragrant herb used widely in Italian cooking.

clue.text: In novel way, including Duke, Queen, or one of their children

indicators.note: including means the phrase surrounds the other letters

parts.note: to do something in a novel way is to do it anew
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A novelist's fresh take on a duke and queen and their offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: D and R go inside ANEW. 'Duke, Queen' recalls Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, and Queen Elizabeth II, whose son is Prince Andrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Andrew is a son of Queen Elizabeth II and the Duke of Edinburgh.

clue.text: Author improvises in play, injecting energy

indicators.note: injecting means putting the energy letter inside the other word

parts.note: musicians who improvise together jam
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A writer ad-libbing on stage, putting real energy into a play.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside JAMS. 'Author' is Henry James, the American-born novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry James wrote The Portrait of a Lady and The Turn of the Screw.

clue.text: Moves finally made to finish off hunted animals

parts.note: to finish something off is to end it
game is animals hunted for sport or food

explanation.surface: Hunters closing in for the kill on their quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is from chess: the last phase of a game, when the final moves are played.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, the final stage of play, with few pieces left, is called the endgame.

clue.text: Atrocious seducer legally challenged

indicators.note: atrocious means dreadfully bad, so the letters of the next word are in a terrible mess

explanation.surface: A dreadful seducer faces a legal challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Atrocious' is the anagram signal working on SEDUCER.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge or juror who is challenged and stands aside from a case is recused.

clue.text: Keep pressure on to answer

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
re means on or concerning, as in business letters
to serve is to answer, as in 'serve the purpose' or 'answer the purpose'

explanation.surface: Keep the pressure on until someone answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'answer' in the sense of being good enough, to serve.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to maintain it or hold onto it unchanged.

clue.text: Dog that's needed on Hebridean island

indicators.note: needed on means the second piece is attached after the first

parts.note: Coll is an island in the Inner Hebrides, off western Scotland
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A dog required on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed on' attaches the abbreviation after the island. The Hebrides are Scotland's western island groups, sheep country where such dogs work.
explanation.definitionFit: A collie is a breed of sheepdog originating in Scotland.

clue.text: See 4
Foreign article about this country in book

indicators.note: about means going round, so the article encloses the country letters

parts.note: le is French for the
UK, the United Kingdom, is this country for a British paper

explanation.surface: A foreign piece written about Britain appears in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the country inside the article. 'book' means a book of the Bible, one of the four Gospels.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gospel according to Luke is the third book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Equation initially given in algebra possibly leading to unknown in nice way

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged otherwise, so they are reordered
initially picks the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: Solving an equation pleasantly, with algebra leading to an unknown quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letter of 'Equation'; 'possibly' rearranges it with the letters of 'algebra'; the unknown letter follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something agreeably is doing it pleasantly or nicely.

clue.text: Battalion is in Germany, some turning into heroes

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A battalion stationed in Germany, some of whom become celebrated as heroes.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts in 'BattaLION' and ends in 'Germany'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lionise people is to treat them as celebrities, making heroes of them.

clue.text: He wrote about infamous gamekeeper catching bird in net, perhaps

indicators.note: catching means holding the bird inside

parts.note: lace is a netlike fabric; net is one kind of it
a wren is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper netting a bird, tied to a notorious literary scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' puts the bird inside. The gamekeeper is Mellors in Lady Chatterley's Lover, banned in Britain for obscenity until 1960.
explanation.definitionFit: D.H. Lawrence wrote Lady Chatterley's Lover, whose hero is the gamekeeper Mellors.

clue.text: Lie given out to persuade in cunning fashion

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lie told to talk someone round by trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LIE GIVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To inveigle is to coax or win someone over through flattery or deception.

clue.text: Soldier tossed a coin, having irrational view of risk

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: tossed means thrown about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A soldier flips a coin, revealing a fearful attitude to chance.
explanation.walkthrough: PARA, then 'tossed' rearranges A COIN into NOIAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A paranoiac person suffers from paranoia, irrational suspicion and fear of threats.

clue.text: Collection of religious verses from Donne, for example

definitions.meaning: a Gospel of the New Testament, its text set out in numbered verses

explanation.surface: Religious verses gathered from the poet Donne.
explanation.walkthrough: John Donne wrote Holy Sonnets, which makes the surface plausible; the answer is the fourth Gospel and his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gospel of John is a book of the Bible, and John Donne was the Metaphysical poet.

clue.text: Bush, for example, English planted in ravine

indicators.note: planted in means put inside

parts.note: a gorge is a deep narrow ravine

explanation.surface: A bush, an English one, planted down in a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside GORGE. 'Bush' is not a shrub but the US president George Bush.
explanation.definitionFit: George W. Bush and his father George H.W. Bush were both US presidents.

clue.text: Rabbit who got the better of wolf in fairy tale?

definitions.meaning: Beatrix Potter's rabbit in the blue jacket

definitions.text: who got the better of wolf in fairy tale?
definitions.meaning: the boy who captures the wolf in Prokofiev's musical tale

explanation.definitionFit: Peter Rabbit is Beatrix Potter's character, and Peter traps the wolf in Prokofiev's Peter and the Wolf.

clue.text: Shrubs out of place in a nursery?

definitions.meaning: small trees bearing elderflowers and elderberries

definitions.text: out of place in a nursery?
definitions.meaning: older people, out of place among small children

explanation.surface: Bushes that do not belong in a plant nursery.
explanation.definitionFit: Elders are shrubs of the genus Sambucus, and elders, the older generation, would be odd in a children's nursery.

clue.text: Artist keen to follow Danton's lead

indicators.note: to follow means the keen word comes after the opening letter
lead here means the leading, opening letter

parts.note: avid means eager or keen

explanation.surface: A painter eager to take a revolutionary leader's lead.
explanation.walkthrough: D, from the start of 'Danton's', then AVID. Jacques-Louis David was the painter of the French Revolution, in which Danton was a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques-Louis David was the leading French neoclassical painter.

clue.text: Prepared to stick males in a seedy club

indicators.note: in means the males sit inside the club word

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar or club
hes are males, as opposed to shes

explanation.surface: Men in a sleazy club ready to stay put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the males inside the club. 'Prepared to stick' is an adjective phrase: ready or able to stick.
explanation.definitionFit: An adhesive substance is one designed to make things stick together.

clue.text: Revere, say, using Asian title of respect in China

indicators.note: in means the title goes inside the friend word

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate, from china plate, so a pal
U is a Burmese honorific, like Mr

explanation.surface: Honouring someone with an Asian courtesy title in China.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside PAL. 'Revere' is not the verb but Paul Revere, the American patriot of the midnight ride; china meaning a mate is Cockney rhyming slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Revere rode to warn of British troops in 1775.

clue.text: Flier introducing new airline's opening in Italian city

parts.note: a raven is a bird, a flier

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of the airline word

explanation.surface: A new airline's inaugural flight to an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: RAVEN, then N, then A from the start of 'airline's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenna is a city in northern Italy famed for its Byzantine mosaics.

clue.text: Catch fish in enclosed space, using some angling equipment

indicators.note: in means the fish sits inside the enclosure word

parts.note: a ring is an enclosed arena, as for boxing or a circus
an eel is a long snakelike fish

explanation.surface: Landing a fish in a confined area with tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the fish inside the enclosure. 'Catch' is a link here; the definition means working a fishing reel.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is part of an angler's tackle, so winding line with it is reeling.

clue.text: He's nearly at the end of balanced diet

indicators.note: nearly at the end of says the letters sit just short of the close of the following words

explanation.surface: A man almost finishing a balanced diet.
explanation.walkthrough: The name straddles 'balancED DIEt', stopping one letter short of the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddie is a man's name, so it can stand for a male person.

clue.text: Romantic song was deceptive?

definitions.meaning: a German art song of the Romantic era, as by Schubert

explanation.definitionFit: A lied is a German Romantic art song, and someone who told falsehoods lied.

clue.text: Monster conger eel sliced up, odd pieces discarded

indicators.note: sliced up means the fish is cut into separate pieces
dropping the odd pieces keeps the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A monstrous conger eel cut up, with stray bits thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: Keeping the even letters of CONGER EEL gives the monster.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore.
